binders: There exists a real constant c, chosen before all subsequent data.
Universally quantified types ι and Ω are equipped respectively with a finite-type structure and a measurable-space structure.
μ is an implicit probability measure on Ω.
X is an implicit family X : ι → Ω → ℝ, and hne proves that the finite index type is nonempty.
For each tail conclusion, t is an arbitrary implicit real threshold subject to 0 ≤ t.
hypotheses: Every component X_i is μ-integrable and centered: ∫ X_i dμ = 0.
Every component gauge q_i = LocalDef003 μ X_i is finite: q_i < ∞.
The family X is jointly independent under μ.
For the ordinary two-regime bound, S = Σ_i (q_i.toReal)² is assumed positive.
For the exceptional bound, S is instead assumed equal to zero.
conclusions: Writing S = Σ_i (q_i.toReal)² and M = max_i q_i.toReal, if S>0 then for every t≥0, μ{|Σ_i X_i|≥t} ≤ 2 exp(-c·min(t²/S, t/M)).
If S=0, then for every t≥0, μ{|Σ_i X_i|≥t} ≤ 2 when t=0 and μ{|Σ_i X_i|≥t} ≤ 0 when t≠0.
mathematical_definitions: A scale q∈ENNReal is admissible for a real-valued function Y under μ when Y is measurable, q≠0, q≠∞, exp(|Y|/q.toReal) is μ-integrable, and ∫exp(|Y|/q.toReal)dμ≤2.
The component gauge q_i is the ENNReal infimum of all admissible scales for X_i.
S is the sum of the squares of all real-valued component gauges.
M is the maximum of the real-valued component gauges over the nonempty finite family.
The probability notation in the conclusions is the real conversion of μ applied to the closed tail event {ω: |Σ_i X_i(ω)|≥t}.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that every nonempty finite jointly independent family of measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables with finite exponential-moment gauges satisfies a two-regime concentration bound. If S, the sum of squared gauges, is positive, then the probability that the absolute value of the family sum is at least t is at most 2 exp(-c min(t²/S,t/M)) for every t≥0, where M is the largest component gauge. If S=0, the proposition instead gives the explicit degenerate bound 2 at t=0 and 0 at every positive threshold.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is required to be finite and nonempty; empty families are excluded.
All components share one probability space and must separately be measurable, integrable, centered, and have finite gauge.
The constant c is existentially quantified before the family and is therefore universal, but no numerical value is specified.
Tail thresholds are restricted to t≥0, and the tail event uses the closed inequality ≥.
The ordinary exponential estimate is conditional on S>0. Under this condition, nonnegativity of the component gauges and nonemptiness imply M>0, although M>0 is not written as a separate hypothesis.
The zero-S conclusion is a separate conditional branch and avoids the real divisions t²/S and t/M.
When S=0 and t≠0, the right side is exactly 0; together with t≥0 this concerns positive thresholds and asserts that the tail event has measure zero.
At S=0 and t=0, the stated upper bound is 2 rather than the sharp probability bound 1.
The definition uses ENNReal.toReal, but the hypotheses exclude infinite component gauges.
The gauge is an infimum and is not required to be attained by an admissible scale.
Because each branch is an implication, a branch is vacuous when its corresponding condition on S fails; mathematically S is a sum of squares and hence cannot be negative.
The proposition itself does not separately state that zero gauge forces a component to vanish almost everywhere; the zero-S tail conclusion supplies the resulting degenerate behavior directly.
